questions.q: Which report format would you choose to show open Requests grouped by both Owner AND Priority at once, as a true cross-tab?
options: Tabular
Summary
Joined
Matrix
questions.explain: A matrix report groups by rows and columns simultaneously, which is exactly the shape of an 'X by Y' cross-tab question.

questions.q: What happens to every dashboard component built on a given report when you change that report's filters?
options: Nothing — dashboard components are independent of their source report once created
Only the first component updates
Every dashboard component built on that report updates, since a dashboard visualizes its source report's results
The dashboard must be manually rebuilt from scratch
questions.explain: A dashboard component doesn't hold its own data — it's a visualization of a source report, so changing the report changes every component built on it.

questions.q: A dashboard needs to be shared across reps and managers, where reps should see only their own records and managers should see their team's. What setting achieves this with a single dashboard?
options: Run the dashboard as a specified admin user for everyone
Set the dashboard to run dynamically as the logged-in user
Create a separate static dashboard for every single user
Disable all sharing rules on the underlying object
questions.explain: A dynamic dashboard (run as logged-in user) applies each viewer's own sharing and field-level security, so one dashboard stays honest for every role.

questions.q: Which report format is the fastest to build but provides no subtotals at all?
options: Tabular
Summary
Matrix
Joined
questions.explain: Tabular reports are a flat list of records with no grouping or subtotal — good for a quick export-style view, not for totals.

questions.q: Why embed a Report Chart or Dashboard component directly on a Lightning app page via Lightning App Builder, instead of leaving it on a separate Reports tab?
options: It is required by Salesforce for all custom objects
It puts the relevant data where the user already is, which is part of what makes an app feel like a finished application rather than a database with a UI
It makes the chart static and unfilterable
It removes the need for any sharing rules on the object
questions.explain: Embedding reports/dashboards directly on the app's own pages means a user doesn't have to go find a separate tab — the current, filtered data is simply there when the app opens.
